summary: Lucentra Health: priority-fallthrough causing multi-region elevated tail latency, streaming resets, and billing exposure - post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC and 2026-03-12 11:35 UTC Lucentra Health experienced elevated tail latency (95th/99th) and intermittent streaming resets for a subset of requests flagged as high-priority. Impact included degraded user-facing response times for clinical note generation and truncated streaming outputs. Customer reported duplicate completions for some requests and saw an unexpected billing spike.

Impact: High (P0) - critical clinical workflow degraded for paying enterprise customer. Multiple downstream retries increased token usage and produced a billing delta.

Environment: Production (hosted) with routing policies that prioritize enterprise traffic to dedicated pools in us-east and eu-west. Dedicated pools are backed by reserved GPU capacity with autoscale for burst.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send high-priority streaming completion request with conversation context X and prompt length ~1k tokens targeting model redwood-v1
2) Observe backend routing decision logs that mark request as 'priority-fallthrough' and route to quantized variant in lower-tier pool
3) Trigger load with 200 concurrent priority requests and watch 95th/99th latency rise and occasional streaming resets
4) Inspect token accounting to see duplicate/retried completions increasing billed tokens
logs: 2026-03-12T09:41:07Z serving-runtime: request_id=rc-9f3b kernel_swap_timeout seq=128 latency=1.9s status=stream_reset
comments: 2026-03-12 09:48 - Priya Menon (Support): Customer reported 'multiple sessions timing out and some outputs truncated mid-stream. Billing shows big increase.' Asked for request IDs and sample transcripts.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Connor Hayes (SRE): Tuned temporary routing override to force Lucentra traffic to reserve-pool-us-east while investigation proceeds. Notified customer of temporary mitigation.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Elena Park (Oncall Eng): Identified mis-evaluation in smart-routing policy: priority fallback rule incorrectly matched when reserve-pool had transient low_capacity metric due to autoscaler lag. Submitted hotfix PR to add hysteresis and capacity grace period.
2026-03-12 13:20 - Lucentra Support Contact (Martin Blake): Confirmed reduced errors and improved streaming after forced override; asked for root cause and compensation for billing spike.
2026-03-13 09:30 - Connor Hayes (SRE): Hotfix rolled to production (canary then global) and routing metrics instrumented. Began billing reconciliation with Finance for affected window.
2026-03-14 08:00 - Priya Menon (Support): Marking ticket for post-incident review; draft action items attached. Customer satisfied with mitigation and asked for playbook updates.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: network blips causing pool health probes to report short-term low_capacity leading routing to fall back to lower-tier pools.

Key finding: autoscaler's capacity_available metric can lag under sustained burst because scale-up request is queued behind priority buckets; smart-routing used immediate capacity_available without tolerance, producing 'priority-fallthrough' for ~13 minutes across bursts in us-east and eu-west.
Secondary finding: serving-runtime kernel swap on quantized variant had higher tail in streaming scenarios (long sequences), which amplified user-visible resets and retries.

Telemetry: Requests tagged priority=high that hit lower-tier pool had 3.2x higher 99th latency and 2.7x higher streaming reset rate during incident window. Token accounting shows ~17% duplicated tokens when clients retried after stream failures.
resolution_notes: Mitigation (short-term): Applied routing override to pin Lucentra traffic to reserve-pool-us-east and reserve-pool-eu-west while teams implemented fix. This restored SLOs within 18 minutes for most sessions.

Fix (hotfix): Updated smart-routing policy to include a capacity_grace_period=30s and hysteresis to prevent immediate fallthrough when capacity_available temporarily drops. Deployed as canary at 2026-03-12T12:45Z and rolled to global by 2026-03-12T13:05Z.

Runtime improvement: Flagged long-sequence streaming on quantized backends and adjusted kernel selection to prefer streaming-optimized kernels for sequences >512 tokens. Deployed small kernel tweak in redwood-quantized-v1 at 2026-03-13.
Billing remediation: Finance issued a one-time credit to Lucentra for the incident window covering duplicated token exposure; adjusted invoice and sent itemized reconciliation on 2026-03-13.
Customer communication: Shared timeline, root cause, and compensation details. Customer accepted remediation and requested a follow-up review with their SREs.
postincident_action_items: 1) Add unit/integration tests for smart-routing policy to simulate autoscaler lag and prevent regressing capacity_grace_period behavior (owner: routing-team, due: 2026-03-26)
2) Update serving-runtime kernel selection tests to include long-sequence streaming workloads and include quantized variants in CI (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-03-20)
3) Create automated alert that detects >=10% rise in duplicate token accounting across a customer cohort within 30 minutes (owner: billing-team, due: 2026-03-19)
4) Update Lucentra runbook with emergency routing override steps and contact list; schedule tabletop with customer for 2026-03-25 (owner: support-ops, due: 2026-03-24)
5) Review autoscaler queueing prioritization and consider fast-path for reserve-pool scale-ups tied to enterprise SLA customers (owner: infra-team, due: 2026-04-02)
6) Postmortem writeup and publish to Confluence; include timeline, dashboards, and mitigations (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2026-03-18)
7) Add explicit billing reconciliation playbook for duplicated-token incidents (owner: finance-ops, due: 2026-03-22)
customer_satisfaction: Customer acknowledged timely mitigation and accepted billing credit. Customer requested a joint runbook tabletop and asked for semi-annual routing policy reviews.
